card.name: Linking verbs before a condition clause
card.fires_on: Short verbs like "is" or "become" right after a subject such as "product", "infusion" or "who", in conditional warnings. The next words describe a state, such as discolored, pregnant or well tolerated.

modes.label: Product condition check
modes.description: "is" after "product" in discard-if-discolored instructions, and the comma in the parenteral inspection sentence.
modes.example: Discard if product<< is>> discolored or contains particulate matter

modes.label: Patients who become
modes.description: "become" after "who" in warnings about patients developing a state like pregnancy or depression.
modes.example: Consideration should be given to removing NEXPLANON in patients who<< become>> significantly depressed.

modes.label: Other conditional verbs
modes.description: "is" or "being" after a subject in an if-clause or outcome clause.
